cost_inputs.estimated_cost_note: Omitted deliberately. docs/runbooks/v3-shadow-evaluation.md forbids writing a cost without an approved pricing reference.

outcomes.note: DECLINED is available to the multi-agent path only: a baseline output schema has no status field and requires at least one prescription. rejected_rate is the architecture-symmetric part.

fairness_conditions.downstream_gate: identical compiler, integrity validator and deterministic fallback
fairness_conditions.embedding: not re-run per architecture; the pool is composed once per case
fairness_conditions.llm_model: identical: one provider object is built once and shared
fairness_conditions.output_schema: identical up to proposal_references and repair_attempt, which only a multi-agent run can supply
fairness_conditions.prompt: the baseline instruction is composed from the four shipped role prompts
fairness_conditions.tool_scope: A sees only the fields the output schema requires; B and C see the same full pool projection
fairness_conditions.user_input: identical: the same EvaluationCase list, in the same order
fairness_conditions.vector_db: identical ExercisePoolSnapshot per case; PostgreSQL decides eligibility

notes: Judge scores are blind and therefore not comparable with the PHASE 5 numbers.
The baselines get no repair round; the multi-agent path does. Every paid multi-agent run in PHASE 4 used zero repairs, so the asymmetry had no measured effect, but it favours C.
A PlanSpec structurally requires three proposal references, so a baseline plan reaches the shipped compiler through a contract adapter that invents no advice. See runners/single_agent.py.
